Authored intent to runtime behavior

Components

Abyssal separates saved ComponentDefinitions from live Components so assets stay reusable and runtime behavior stays explicit.

This reference lists the real component capabilities currently recognized or implemented by the engine. Not every documented component can be added through Wings Assembler.

ComponentDefinition

Serializable behavior intent authored and saved with an asset. Today this is root-level Tag, Resource, and Team data on FragmentAssets.

Runtime Component

A live capability attached to an Actor during instantiation or gameplay. Runtime Components are not saved directly into reusable asset files.

Component Catalog

The metadata registry describing component identity, category, availability, persistence, and documentation relationships.

Factory Boundary

The translation point that applies saved definitions to live Actors. Tag adds Actor tags; Resource and Team create or update live Components.

Design Rule

Assets store what should exist. Runtime systems decide how that intent becomes behavior in the current world or match.

Status Legend

Authorable Runtime Planned Internal

Authorable means the current Wings Assembler Add Component workflow can save it as a ComponentDefinition. Runtime means implemented and used by gameplay, but not directly authored on Fragments yet.

Authorable Components

Tag

Authorable

Adds identity labels to a Fragment root. Tags let systems recognize groups such as player objects, enemies, fighter units, or damageable objects without depending on a specific class.

Authored fields
Enabled, Tags. Tags are written as a comma-separated list in Wings Assembler and saved as normalized strings.
Saved definition
Tag ComponentDefinition.
Runtime result
The factory adds the saved tags to the instantiated Actor. It does not create a live Tag Component object.
Example
Unit.Fighter.Heavy, Actor.Enemy, Damageable.

Resource

Authorable

Defines a named value such as Health, Energy, Shield, Fuel, or Ammunition. Gameplay can reduce, restore, spend, or inspect that value at runtime.

Authored fields
Enabled, Resource Id, Maximum, Starting Value.
Saved definition
Resource ComponentDefinition.
Runtime result
The factory creates or reuses a Resource Component on the live Actor and adds the named resource.
Example
A Fragment can define Health with maximum 150 and starting value 150.

Team

Authorable

Defines the default ownership team for a Fragment root. Team is used by targeting, projectile rules, faction materials, and ally/enemy checks.

Authored fields
Enabled, Team ID. Current IDs are Neutral, Player, Enemy, and Ally.
Saved definition
Team ComponentDefinition.
Runtime result
The factory creates or reuses a Team Component on the live Actor and sets the authored team.
Ownership rule
Fragment-authored Team is a default for direct placement. Explicit match, recipe, or spawn context can override it at runtime.

Runtime Components

Weapon

Runtime

Stores weapon slots, active weapon, damage, range, cooldown, and firing checks. Current recipe/runtime configuration supplies weapons; Fragment authoring for reusable weapon definitions is deferred.

Developer name: WeaponComponent.

Projectile State

Runtime

Moves a projectile Actor, tracks owner, velocity, lifetime, and hit behavior. Projectiles are temporary runtime effects and are not saved into Fragment assets.

Developer name: ProjectileComponent.

Base Production

Runtime

Represents base ownership, account identity, lane association, spawn metadata, health monitoring, and destruction behavior. It is active in gameplay, but authoring base capability separately from runtime owner/account/lane data is future work.

Developer name: BaseComponent.

Mesh Renderer

Internal

Connects a Mesh and Material to a visual Actor so the renderer can draw it. Designers author mesh nodes and material references instead of adding Mesh Renderer as a ComponentDefinition.

Developer name: MeshRenderer.

Possession

Runtime

Marks a runtime Actor as possessable and stores the current owner id. The play-mode possession workflow owns this today; placed-instance or construct authoring may come later.

Developer name: PossessionComponent.

Camera Target

Runtime

Stores camera follow target settings for possessable Actors. It is not part of Fragment authoring yet.

Developer name: CameraTargetComponent.

Ability

Runtime

Stores runtime ability entries, cooldowns, resource costs, and activation callbacks. Ability data needs a stable asset definition before it becomes authorable.

Developer name: AbilityComponent.

Effect

Runtime

Applies resource changes to a target, optionally modified by Element data. Effects are implemented, but reusable authored effect definitions are deferred.

Developer name: EffectComponent.

Element

Runtime

Stores elemental affinities or amounts such as Physical, Light, Fire, or Void. It is a likely future Fragment identity capability, but it has no stable authoring format yet.

Developer name: ElementComponent.

Inventory

Runtime

Stores runtime item stacks and item metadata. Starting inventory and save rules are not defined yet, so it is not authorable.

Developer name: InventoryComponent.

Internal Engine State

Internal

Transform, Script, Actor Identity, and Wings Assembler preview state are engine-owned concepts. They are documented so the boundary is clear, but designers do not add them as Fragment ComponentDefinitions.

Behaviors

Lane Movement

Runtime

Moves units through a lane corridor, approaches combat targets in 2D, holds weapon range, and applies lightweight friendly separation. It depends on lane data, Team, Targeting, and Weapon state.

Developer name: LanePushBehavior.

Auto Combat

Runtime

Aims at the current target, asks the Weapon component to fire, and sends successful shots through the projectile system. It depends on Targeting, Weapon, Resource, and Projectile systems.

Developer name: AutoCombatBehavior.

Movement

Runtime

Generic movement behavior for forward, chase, flee, and orbit motion. It is implemented as runtime code and not exposed as a saved Fragment definition.

Developer name: MovementBehavior.

Follow

Runtime

Moves one Actor near another runtime target, with optional teleporting when too far away. Runtime target references are not reusable asset data.

Developer name: FollowBehavior.

Player Input

Runtime

Consumes input actions and axes for movement, weapons, and abilities. It is attached by possession/runtime systems, not authored directly on a Fragment.

Developer name: PlayerInputBehavior.

Patrol

Runtime

Moves an Actor between patrol points. The behavior exists, but route authoring belongs to future scene or placed-instance tools rather than reusable Fragment identity.

Developer name: PatrolBehavior.

Spawner

Runtime

Can spawn Actors from a configured factory with alive limits and respawn delay. Public authoring is deferred until spawn targets, ownership, and recipes have a stable data model.

Developer name: SpawnerBehavior.

Sensors

Targeting Sensor

Runtime

Finds and maintains a valid target by range and team relationship. Auto Combat and Lane Movement consume the target it finds.

Developer name: TargetingSensor.

Distance Sensor

Runtime

Tracks whether a runtime target is inside or outside enter/exit distance thresholds and emits callbacks when that state changes.

Developer name: DistanceComponent.

Controllers

Construct Purchase

Runtime

Coordinates AI or commander-driven construct purchasing. It checks economy balance, consults a purchase strategy, respects pending paid-unit pressure, and sends valid requests to the purchase/deployment services.

Developer name: ConstructPurchaseControllerComponent. This is a runtime commander capability, not a Fragment authoring option.

Runtime but Not Yet Authorable

These systems exist in code or gameplay configuration, but they are not available in the Wings Assembler Add Component dropdown. Their future authoring model still needs stable asset or placed-instance rules.
